title: Understanding, bliss (2.4–2.5)
hook: the Taittiriya goes two layers deeper, through understanding, and finds at the center a self made of joy
tomorrow: "words and mind turn back from it"

segments.voice: Yesterday: breath, and your line, pranamaya, manomaya. The self made of breath, and inside it, the self made of mind. When your mind raced, which changed first, the breath or the thought? Day three hundred ninety-three.

Some maps of the inner life end somewhere dark. Peel back the polite surface of a person, those stories go, and you'll find fear, or hunger, or a scared animal. The Taittiriya Upanishad peels back the layers too. Food, then breath, then mind. And it keeps going, two more layers, down to the very center. What it finds there is the surprise of the whole chapter. Not fear. Not a void. Joy. Today, the last two layers, and the claim that a person's deepest layer is made of bliss.
screen: `PEEL BACK A PERSON. WHAT'S THERE?` → `FOOD, BREATH, MIND.` → `TWO MORE LAYERS.`

segments.voice: Section four. Inside the self made of mind, the text says, is a self made of understanding. Vijnanamaya. One way to hear the difference: mind, yesterday, was the part that learns and repeats; understanding sees what the learning is for, and acts on it. The text draws it, like the others, as a bird. Faith, shraddha, is its head. Rita, the right order of things, is one wing. Satya, truth, is the other. Yoga is its body. And mahas, greatness, is its tail. Faith at the head is worth a second look. In this text, understanding doesn't start from doubt. It starts from trust, and grows into truth. The text even says understanding carries out the sacrifice and every action, and the gods themselves honor it as Brahman. Then section five. Inside understanding is a self made of bliss. Anandamaya. Its head is priya, what is dear. One wing is moda, delight. The other is pramoda, great delight. Its body is ananda, bliss itself. And its tail, the ground it rests on, is Brahman. So at the very center, the Upanishad finds joy, resting on the ground of everything. Here the teachers of Vedanta disagree, and the disagreement is old. Shankara read the bliss-self as still one more layer, with Brahman as its foundation underneath. Other teachers, reading a line in the Brahma Sutras, held that the self made of bliss is Brahman itself. Both readings agree on the direction. Go inward far enough, and what you meet is not dread. It's ananda.
screen: `INSIDE MIND, A SELF MADE OF UNDERSTANDING.` · `ITS HEAD IS FAITH; ITS WINGS, ORDER AND TRUTH.` · `INSIDE THAT, A SELF MADE OF BLISS.` · `ITS FOUNDATION IS BRAHMAN.` · then, large: `ANANDAMAYA.`

segments.voice: Two minutes going inward. Feel the body, then the breath, then the chatter of the mind. Don't fight it. Just let it run a little farther off, like a radio in another room. Now notice whatever is noticing all of that. It doesn't need to do anything. And see if there's anything there, even faintly, like ease. It might be tiny: the relief of sitting down, the warmth of your own hands. If something like that shows up, rest in it. If it doesn't, rest anyway. The bell holds the time.
Understanding. Vijnana, the fourth layer in the Taittiriya: faith at its head, order and truth for wings, and inside it, the self made of bliss.
Your line: the innermost is joy. Today, when someone is short with you, try the Taittiriya's map on them: under the food, the breath and the mood, joy is the center. Day three hundred ninety-three.

screen: `DAY 393 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WORDS AND MIND TURN BACK.`

howItsDone: In Vedanta study, students learn the five layers in order, food to bliss, and teachers often use them as a guided meditation that moves attention inward from the body to the quiet center.

match.prompt: the last two layers — tap the pairs.

myth: in the Taittiriya, the innermost self is made of bliss
anandamaya: inside understanding, a self made of joy, resting on Brahman.
all Vedanta teachers agree the bliss-self is Brahman itself
Shankara read it as one more layer, with Brahman beneath; others read it as Brahman.
its head is shraddha, faith. truth and right order are its wings.

fork.setup: you peel back the layers of a person: food, breath, mind, understanding. what does the Taittiriya say is at the center?
fork.reveal: anandamaya: a self made of bliss, with what is dear as its head and Brahman as its foundation.

original.note: Sanskrit ānandamaya: ānanda, bliss, + maya, made of. the fifth and innermost self in Taittiriya 2.5.

trapdoor: what you thought: the deepest part of a person is the scared part.
what it means: in the Taittiriya, the innermost layer is a self made of bliss, resting on Brahman.
what a scholar hears: Brahma Sutra 1.1.12, ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt, and the long Vedanta debate over whether the bliss-self is Brahman or a last sheath with Brahman as its ground.

notes: Parts given from memory: vijnanamaya (shraddha head, rta right, satya left, yoga body, mahas tail); anandamaya (priya head, moda right, pramoda left, ananda body, brahma tail/foundation). Please confirm.
'Understanding carries out the sacrifice and every action, and the gods honor it as Brahman' paraphrases the verse opening 2.5 (vijnanam yajnam tanute...); confirm placement.

The anandamaya debate: Shankara's commentary on Brahma Sutra 1.1.12ff reads the bliss-self as a sheath with Brahman as its 'tail' (support); other teachers take anandamaya as Brahman. Described without naming schools beyond Shankara; a Keeper may want to name them.
The opening 'old story' about fear at the center is a general picture, not attributed to any tradition.
Editor review (2026-10-01): softened the opening 'most maps of the inner life' generalization and framed the mind/understanding contrast as one reading, not the text's statement.
